title: Connexions de Gauss-Manin et équations de Picard-Fuchs. Opération de Cartier : copies de tapuscrit annoté (s.d.), tiré à part (1981), notes manuscrites (s.d.).

errors: Self-referential slip: 'l'élément de structure d) est connu dans b) et d)' should read 'dès b) et c)' (b and c determine d).
Gap: Deligne's theorem is stated for vector bundles with connection; applying it to a PGL_2-bundle needs the G-bundle version or a local lift. This is standard but not stated.

Gap: algebraicity of the section σ (c) does not follow from Deligne's theorem on (a),(b) alone. One needs moderate growth of σ, or an argument identifying σ with a canonical algebraic sub-line-bundle (e.g. via jets of T^{-1/2}). The marginal claim '(impliquant l'algébricité de c)' is unjustified on the page, though true for the uniformizing oper.

ideas.what: Encoding the uniformization of a Riemann surface as a canonical P^1-bundle with flat connection and section over X
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical: Poincaré, Klein, Fuchs; bundle formulation Gunning (1966-67); opers Drinfeld–Sokolov (1985), Beilinson–Drinfeld (1990s)

ideas.what: Transversality condition: σ nowhere stationary for c_X, and then (b)+(c) determine a formal isomorphism from the completion of P_X along σ to the completion of X×X along the diagonal
ideas.modern_name: Oper transversality; an oper determines the formal developing map (projective structure via jets / neighbourhood of the diagonal)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Gunning; Deligne (Équations différentielles..., 1970, projective connections); Beilinson–Drinfeld

ideas.what: Algebraicity of the uniformizing structure on a non-proper algebraic curve via Riemann–Hilbert with regular singularities
ideas.modern_name: Deligne's Riemann–Hilbert correspondence applied to the uniformizing oper (regular singular at the cusps)

missed.claim: Grothendieck proposes to obtain existence/uniqueness of the algebraic uniformizing data (P_X, c_X, σ, p_X) 'par une autre voie', i.e. without Deligne's theorem. On the next page he asks for a purely algebraic description of σ and p_X. This is essentially an algebraic characterization of the uniformizing oper among all opers (the accessory-parameter problem). It remains open in general and is not settled here.
missed.quote: Mais nous allons étudier l'existence (et établir l'unicité), et préciser ce pb d'existence - par une autre voie
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Shows Grothendieck framing uniformization in essentially oper language, in the same dossier as Gauss–Manin/Cartier. This is suggestive for p-adic/arithmetic analogues (Mochizuki's p-adic Teichmüller theory uses exactly dormant/indigenous bundles). The underlying mathematics is however classical.

deep.surprise_reason: The content is the classical uniformizing projective structure, recast as (P^1-bundle, flat connection, nowhere-stationary section, formal developing iso). This is precisely the indigenous bundle/oper formalism later made central by Gunning, Beilinson–Drinfeld and Mochizuki. It is mildly interesting to see Grothendieck use it in this form, alongside Cartier-operator material, but no new result is established.
